summary: Point Mountain (Potato Knob) fire tower above Webster Springs, Webster County, West Virginia; built 1925 or 1927 (sources differ), 100 ft after 1965; standing, not regularly staffed.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 tower with a 7 by 7 foot cab, 60 feet originally and extended by 40 feet in 1965; concrete block observer's cabin added near the base in 1952

staffing.status: not regularly staffed; maintained for emergencies

events.note: State spent $81 on a contract to establish a lookout structure (WV Forest, Game and Fish Warden Biennial Report 1913-14, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Watchman posted at the station, living 12 miles away and staying there each night; seven miles of telephone line built to the station
Register: built by the West Virginia Conservation Commission as a 60-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower
A 1973 Charleston Gazette article, as quoted by Forest Lookouts, says the tower was originally built to 60 feet in 1927. Conflicts with the Register's 1925.
Concrete block observer's cabin added near the base
Blind observer E.D. Harrison relayed fire reports during deer season; a helper spotted smoke for him (Post Herald-Register, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)
40-foot section added, bringing the tower to 100 feet
Registered September 10, 1998; nominated by Ralph P. Glover, Jr., Deputy State Forester

corrections.current: FFLOS US 1692 linked to this tower
corrections.proposed: FFLOS US 1692 kept as a separate Potato Hill record, unlinked until the nominator confirms the same site
corrections.why: The FFLOS entry places its tower at an unknown location in Webster County and lists no coordinates, so it cannot be tied to this tower's coordinates. The FFLOS registration date (2017) is therefore not evidence for this tower.

notes_for_editor: Build year conflicts: the NHLR says 1925 (WV Conservation Commission); the 1973 Charleston Gazette, quoted by Forest Lookouts, says the tower was originally built to 60 feet in 1927. Both kept as events. Elevation conflicts: NHLR 3,364 ft (matches record elevation_m 1025.3); the 1973 article says 3,500 ft; the 1916 report quoted by Forest Lookouts says 3,550 ft. Not reconciled. Record height_m 30.5 matches the NHLR's 100-foot total height, so it is kept. Registration correction: FFLOS US 1692 ('Potato Hill Tower Site', registered 2017) gives its location as unknown in Webster County with coordinates unlisted, and Forest Lookouts uses the name Potato Hill as a historic name for this site. Whether the FFLOS tower is this one is not established; the correction proposes unlinking, and the 2017 fflos_registered event was left out of this tower's events for that reason. Access and current condition: the newest sources are the NHLR (undated) and the firelookout.org list; the NHLR links to a 2015 video of a climb; no source read says whether the public may visit or climb now. Searches found no 2024-2025 access notice. The WBOY article on climbable WV towers does not mention Point Mountain. Ownership: the NHLR names the WV Division of Forestry as administrator; the Monongahela National Forest list in a search summary was not read and was not used. Budget: four fetch_text page reads (NHLR, FFLOS, firelookout WV list, WBOY), one failed fetch of a WV tower list PDF (DNS error), two WebSearch calls, and one local read of the cached Forest Lookouts page (eastern_us_lookouts/point-mountain.html). No photos added.
